Daily rules for the upbeat handover
Everyone on the desk should know the plain rules
Companion Animal Travel Desk Operations
This section sets the daily standards for safe, calm handling, clear checks, and steady handover work for animals traveling through Aurelia Skyways.
The desk team should greet each traveler with a steady tone, confirm the booking details, and guide owners through crate, feeding, and document checks without hurry. Animals must be handled with quiet movements and humane methods at every stage, and the workstation should stay organized so that notes, tags, and forms are easy to find. When an animal arrives, the team should review fitness for travel, notice signs of stress, and escalate concerns before acceptance if anything seems unclear.
For bird movements, <<FACT F077>> The team should also confirm that the health certificate is current before acceptance, because the paperwork must match the trip and the animal must be fit to fly. <<FACT F083>> Any gap in the record should be raised to the senior coordinator at once, and no animal should be accepted until the documents are in order.
For reptile bookings, <<FACT F066>> This limit protects the animal, the crate, and the handlers, so the desk should verify the stated weight and compare it with the booking record before release to the ramp team. If the crate looks unsafe, the animal should remain with the owner until a safer setup is provided.
During flight, the cabin team monitors animals and reports any change in condition, while the desk keeps the record chain clear so the handover stays traceable from check-in to arrival. If a traveler asks for guidance, the reply should stay simple, calm, and factual.
For any unusual case, contact the duty supervisor or the animal operations lead at once, and keep the Companion Animal Travel Desk informed through the normal handover log.
